objective: Measure repeated connection timing and volume across bounded windows, compare competing scheduled-service explanations, and avoid labeling periodicity alone as command and control.
preconditions: a trusted endpoint or peer and anchor time exist
multiple bounded windows fit inside the authorization envelope
deployed flow and timeline field catalogs are available
required_evidence: timestamp series exact window filters and successful coverage
peer tuple duration byte packet and outcome distributions
asset process DNS TLS or HTTP context when available
positive_evidence: covered multi-window observations show repeatable intervals with stable attributable peer and transfer characteristics
cross-sensor application context contradicts expected scheduled-service explanations
negative_evidence: successful covered windows tie the periodic traffic to an approved updater monitor or persistent application
interval and volume variation plus user or service context refute an automated beacon hypothesis
escalation_pivots: compare an adjacent bounded flow window without changing filters
correlate DNS TLS HTTP and process context for the same peer
request human review when sample coverage is too short for periodicity claims

query_templates.purpose: Collect bounded flow timestamps and volumes for one authorized endpoint-peer relationship.
Correlate periodic flow observations with bounded DNS protocol alert and endpoint context.

alternative_hypotheses: scheduled updater telemetry or health check
persistent messaging VPN or management channel
user-driven activity that appears periodic in a bounded sample
stop_conditions: timing volume peer and application context discriminate the hypotheses
additional windows repeat the same evidence without changing a hypothesis
coverage or sample size prevents periodicity claims
a query budget or deadline is exhausted
confidence_limiters: shared proxy NAT or CDN peer
